topics.title: Reading & Writing Decimals to 3 Places
topics.concept:
What is a Decimal?

A decimal is a way to show numbers less than 1 using a decimal point (•). The decimal point separates whole numbers from parts of a whole.

Place Value Chart:

HundredsTensOnes•TenthsHundredthsThousandths
100101•1/101/1001/1000
003•425

Reading Decimals:

  • 0.425 = "four hundred twenty-five thousandths"
  • 3.7 = "three and seven tenths"
  • 5.082 = "five and eighty-two thousandths"

Writing Decimals:

  • "Six and fifteen hundredths" = 6.15
  • "Two hundred thirty-four thousandths" = 0.234

examples.solution:
• Whole number part: 25 = "twenty-five"
  • Decimal part: 406 thousandths
  • Complete: "Twenty-five and four hundred six thousandths"

• "Eight" = 8
  • "fifteen thousandths" = 0.015
  • Complete: 8.015 (not 8.15, which is fifteen hundredths!)

recap: Decimal point separates whole from part
Always say "and" for the decimal point when reading

topics.title: Rounding Decimals
topics.concept:
What is Rounding?

Rounding makes numbers easier to work with by finding the closest "nice" number.

Steps to Round Decimals:

  1. Find the place value you're rounding to (tenths, hundredths)
  2. Look at the digit to the right
  3. If it's 5 or more → round UP
  4. If it's 4 or less → round DOWN (stay same)

Rounding to Tenths:

  • 3.47 → Look at hundredths place (7 ≥ 5) → round up → 3.5
  • 3.42 → Look at hundredths place (2 ≤ 4) → round down → 3.4

Rounding to Hundredths:

  • 5.673 → Look at thousandths place (3 ≤ 4) → round down → 5.67
  • 5.678 → Look at thousandths place (8 ≥ 5) → round up → 5.68

      ▼       ▼       ▼
      ├───────┼───────┤
      │       │       │

ROUNDING DECISION TREE:

    Start: Find rounding place
              │
              ▼
    Look at digit to the right
              │
        ┌─────┴─────┐
        ▼           ▼
    Is it ≥ 5?   Is it ≤ 4?
        │           │
        ▼           ▼
    Round UP    Round DOWN
    (add 1)     (stay same)

examples.solution:
• Tenths place: 3 (7.3__)
  • Look at hundredths: 4
  • 4 ≤ 4 → round down
  • Answer: 7.3

• Hundredths place: 6 (12.56_)
  • Look at thousandths: 7
  • 7 ≥ 5 → round up (6 becomes 7)
  • Answer: 12.57

• Tenths place: 9 (0.9__)
  • Look at hundredths: 9
  • 9 ≥ 5 → round up (9 becomes 10, carry over)
  • 0.9 + 0.1 = 1.0
  • Answer: 1.0

recap: Rounding to tenths → look at hundredths
Rounding to hundredths → look at thousandths

topics.title: Comparing Decimals
topics.concept:
How to Compare Decimals:

Method 1: Use Place Value

  1. Compare whole numbers first
  2. If whole numbers are equal, compare tenths
  3. If tenths are equal, compare hundredths
  4. Continue to thousandths if needed

Method 2: Use Common Denominator

  • 0.8 = 8/10 = 80/100
  • 0.79 = 79/100
  • 80/100 > 79/100, so 0.8 > 0.79

Method 3: Use Number Line

  • Numbers to the right are greater

examples.problem:
Compare: 0.8 and 0.79

Solution (Place Value):

  • 0.8 = 0.80 (add zero to compare)
  • Compare tenths: 8 vs 7
  • 8 > 7, so 0.8 > 0.79

examples.solution:
• Write with same places: 3.250
  • Compare: 3.245 vs 3.250
  • Hundredths: 4 vs 5 → 4 < 5
  • So 3.245 < 3.25

recap: Add zeros to make same number of decimal places
Compare left to right (whole → tenths → hundredths → thousandths)
